Our work revealed that the HIB1-auxin module regulates root gravitropism and RSA, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying adaptive root growth.

title: The CitRWP–CsWUS regulatory axis governs citrus plant regeneration in association with chromatin remodeling
authors:
Yin Zhou, 
Xietian Song, 
Nan Wang, 
Zhenghua Jiang, 
Yizhang Chen, 
Zongzhou Xie, 
Lijun Chai, 
Xiaomeng Wu, 
Qiang Xu, 
Junli Ye, 
Xiuxin Deng
abstract:
Working model of the  CitRWP–CsWUS  regulatory axis in association with chromatin remodeling in citrus.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Plant regeneration underpins crop genetic improvement, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly characterized in woody fruit trees. The RWP-RK domain-containing (RKD) transcription factor  CitRWP  acts as a pleiotropic regulator of nucellar polyembryony and somatic embryogenesis (SE) in citrus, but its downstream molecular network remains elusive.
We demonstrate that CsWUS, a core stem cell regulator, is a direct downstream target of CitRWP. CitRWP binds to the  CsWUS  promoter to activate its transcription. Additionally, CitRWP interacts with the SWItch/Sucrose Non-Fermentable (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodeling ATPase SPLAYED (SYD), synergistically enhancing  CsWUS  activation, while chromatin accessibility at the  CsWUS  locus is enhanced upon  CitRWP  overexpression. We further uncover that CsWUS negatively regulates  CitRWP  expression via a feedback loop.
 CsWUS  overexpression promotes SE in recalcitrant citrus callus, but causes abnormal meristem proliferation and impairs shoot organogenesis from epicotyl segments.  CsWUS  greatly enhanced  in planta  transformation efficiency in the model citrus.
This study establishes the  CitRWP – CsWUS  regulatory axis as a central module that coordinates multiple developmental fate transitions in association with chromatin remodeling, providing novel insights into the mechanisms of cellular totipotency and plant regeneration.

title: How to build a shoot: insights from Physcomitrium patens
authors:
Simon A. Howe, 
Laura A. Moody
abstract:
Cladogram of the streptophytes illustrating the diversity of apical growth mechanisms in this group.
 
 
 Summary 
 The evolution of body plans with multiple cell layers provided structural rigidity and enabled tissue specialisation, which were both essential for the colonisation of land by plants. Building such structure requires apical cell divisions that generate merophytes along all three axes (3D growth), as well as the spatial control of cell fate. The shoot (gametophore) of the moss  Physcomitrium patens  is an ideal model for studying these processes. Recent studies have identified a genetic network integrating hormone signalling, cell wall biosynthesis and cell shape to regulate division orientation in the gametophore. Additionally, reporter-based markers have revealed localised hormone activity that maintains the gametophore apical cell. This review summarises these findings to provide an updated perspective on 3D growth in  Physcomitrium patens .

title: Navigating through complexity: a roadmap to disentangle multi‐level drivers of intraspecific seed‐trait variability and prioritise research efforts
authors:
Roberta L. C. Dayrell, 
Efisio Mattana, 
Pablo Gómez Barreiro, 
Richard Buggs, 
Michael D. Charters, 
Udayangani Liu, 
Michael Renton, 
Phoebe Swift, 
Ted Chapman, 
Charlotte E. Seal
abstract:
Examples of hierarchical drivers of intraspecific variation in seed traits.







Summary
Seed traits underpin plant regeneration and are central to predicting species' responses to environmental change, yet their intraspecific variability remains poorly integrated into trait‐based frameworks. Progress has been limited by the conflation of processes operating across nested levels, from regions and populations to mother plants and individual seeds, and by weak integration of genetic drivers with environmental and phenotypic data. Drawing on published literature and analyses of seed traits in wild tree populations, we show that substantial seed‐trait variation can occur among mother plants and individual seeds within populations, meaning that population‐level macroenvironmental variables often capture only part of the observed variation. To address these limitations, we propose a roadmap to disentangle hierarchical drivers of intraspecific trait variability (ITV) in seeds. We outline a strategic plan to quantify seed‐trait variation across hierarchical levels, investigate its drivers where variation is concentrated, and assess its consequences for recruitment and demographic outcomes. We recommend coordinated, standardised sampling and experiments that retain mother‐plant and individual‐seed identity, integrate genetic, environmental and phenotypic data, and use scalable approaches to link seed traits to performance across recruitment stages. Recognising and integrating ITV across nested levels is essential for improving predictions of plant regeneration under environmental change.

title: Jasmonate control of barley grain size across generations
authors:
M. D. Nodine, 
G. W. van Esse
abstract: New Phytologist, EarlyView.

title: MaizeGP: An open graph‐based maize pangenome platform for integrative multi‐scale exploration of structural variation
authors:
Nianhua Jia, 
Xianyan Kuang, 
Yueli Wang, 
Wei Song, 
Yan Du, 
Yuhang Guo, 
Yuanhao Guo, 
Chungen Yi, 
Zeyang Ma, 
Shaojiang Chen, 
Junjie Fu, 
Wenxin Liu
abstract: MaizeGP, an interactive graph‐based pangenome platform, integrates structural variation from 48 diverse maize genomes with functional annotations and visualization tools. MaizeGP enables multi‐scale exploration of genomic variation across individual loci, gene families, and trait associations. This accessible resource supports future investigation of maize genome diversity and its biological implications.

title: PbAGO4‐dependent hypermethylation of the PbNAC71 promoter regulates anthocyanin synthesis in pear
authors:
Yansong Zhu, 
Xinyu Li, 
Chen Yang, 
Wenjun Liu, 
Qi Zou, 
Lei Yu, 
Nan Wang, 
Xuesen Chen, 
Zongying Zhang
abstract:
In red pear, light induces  PbNAC71  expression by keeping a promoter enhancer unmethylated. PbAGO4 methylates this enhancer, silencing  PbNAC71 . PbNAC71 and PbMYB10 promote anthocyanin gene expression, producing red color. In the green bud mutant, enhancer hypermethylation blocks this pathway and thereby prevents anthocyanin accumulation.

  
 ABSTRACT 
 Bud mutations in perennial fruit trees often involve epigenetic variation, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We identified a spontaneous green bud mutant of the red-skinned pear “Aohong No. 1” that fails to accumulate anthocyanins under light. Integrated methylome and transcriptome analyses revealed that in the mutant, hypermethylation of a 148-bp light-responsive enhancer in the  PbNAC71  promoter, maintained by PbAGO4, represses  PbNAC71  expression. In the wild type, this enhancer remains hypomethylated, whereas in the mutant, it is hypermethylated; this differential methylation is detectable at the young fruit stage and stably maintained at the post-harvest stages examined, representing a pre-set epigenetic state. Silencing of  PbNAC71  downregulated  PbMYB10  and  PbCHI1 , and attenuated PbMYB10-mediated activation of  PbCHS1  and  PbDFR3 , thereby suppressing anthocyanin accumulation. Both  PbAGO4  knockout in callus and  PbAGO4  silencing in fruit peel reduced enhancer methylation, and increased  PbNAC71  expression and anthocyanin accumulation. Together, these results reveal a mechanism by which PbAGO4-dependent methylation of a light-responsive enhancer establishes a stable pre-set state that controls how environmental light signals regulate anthocyanin synthesis.

title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning
abstract:
Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted structures and amino acid sequences. Within DeepEST, we integrate these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduce a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These choices are well suited for bacteria, in which functionally related genes frequently colocalize and are cotranscribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as informative, condition-dependent signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Averaged over the 25 species, DeepEST reaches a protein-centric
                     F 
                     max 
                    of 0.689 and a term-centric micro-AUPRC of 0.756, a relative improvement of 4.4% and 11.6% over the second-best method, the structure-based predictor DeepFRI. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, supporting their experimental characterization. DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data.

title: Spaceborne radiation-tolerant atomic-layer memory with on-orbit real-time testing
abstract: Abstract The human endeavor in space exploration has never ceased, where space electronics with high radiation tolerance are of paramount importance. Due to the atomic-level thin-layer characteristic, atomic-layer material electronic devices exhibit extremely high radiation tolerance compared with traditional bulk material devices. However, on-orbit testing on atomic-layer electronics is still lacking, restricting the understanding of their online performance in the space environment. Here we report a spaceborne radiation-tolerant and low-noise atomic-layer MoS 2  memory array. Deployed on the Fudan No.1 Satellite in a low Earth orbit, this work enables the first demonstration of on-orbit real-time testing on atomic-layer memory. To date, after 23 months of on-orbit testing, the accuracy of the returned memory data has remained at 100%, indicating impressive radiation tolerance. This work presents a substantial step forward for the practical application of atomic-layer space electronics.

title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections
abstract: Abstract Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers’choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

title: DeSCENT: Deconvolutional Single-Cell RNA-seq Enhances Transcriptome-based Cancer Survival Analysis
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Single-cell RNA-seq captures tumor heterogeneity, but it is rarely available together with patient survival outcomes. Bulk RNA-seq cohorts provide survival data but lack direct measurements of cellular expression. Results DeSCENT generates reference-informed cellular profiles from bulk RNA-seq and combines both representations for survival prediction. We evaluated DeSCENT with three survival models on eight TCGA cancer cohorts. Compared with Bulk, DeSCENT improved average C-index and generally improved time-dependent AUC, while integrated Brier score results were mixed. External validation showed higher average C-index than all three baselines, although performance was lower than in internal evaluation. These findings support the use of cellular representations in the evaluated transcriptome-only setting. Availability and implementation Code:  https://github.com/YonghaoZhao722/DeSCENT . Archival snapshot:  doi:10.5281/zenodo.22073099 . Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.
