Roost makes this evidence, along with genome analyses, accessible to researchers and conservation practitioners, connecting documented disease with host biology and highlighting priorities for sequencing and functional research. Roost is available at http://josephguhlin.com/Roost

title: Deterministic DNA-first discovery reveals recurrent genomic architectures
authors: Hu, G., Wang, H., Yau, S. S.-T.
abstract: Genome mining typically begins with known genes or protein families, which can make systems defined primarily by genomic organization difficult to detect. We developed a DNA-first framework combining asymmetric-covariance natural-vector representations with generic positional recurrence, joining separately calibrated signals through genomic coordinates. In benchmarks of array-associated reverse transcriptase (ART) loci, the target-free mathematical arm localized seven of eight predeclared loci, including all seven with exact-array coordinates. Dual-arm signals occurred in none of three non-array RT controls and in one of five UG27 systems, indicating selectivity within these small control sets. A separate profile-guided search of 6.12 Gb identified five candidate array-associated RT-like systems. In an independent 54.38-Gb evaluation of this profile-guided arm, structural compatibility was 24/32 under a historical-rule mirror, 12/32 after novelty-only selection, and 0/17 for architecture-selected complete ORFs; the two 32-member panels shared six exact sequences. Together, these results suggest that mathematical features of raw DNA can complement protein-directed searches in nominating genomic architectures for experimental RNA-to-DNA studies.

title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Cellular and Molecular Features of Steroid-Induced Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head Compared to Alcohol-Induced Osteonecrosis and Hip Osteoarthritis
authors: Sarkar, A., Gallo, M. C., Bell, J. A., Mayfield, C. K., Ball, J. R., Hernandez, F., Lechtholz-Zey, E., Shelby, T., Sugiyama, O., Evseenko, D., Lieberman, J. R.
abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) remains a devastating complication of glucocorticoid therapy and alcohol abuse, yet the pathophysiology is poorly understood. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we analyzed femoral head specimens from patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty due to steroid-induced ONFH, alcohol-induced ONFH, or hip osteoarthritis (OA). Our comprehensive analysis across conditions revealed etiology-specific cellular compositions and transcriptional profiles. Steroid-induced ONFH demonstrated a distinctive immunological signature characterized by a neutrophil-predominant, elevated innate-to-adaptive immune cell ratio compared to alcohol-induced ONFH or OA. T cell analysis revealed impaired maturation in steroid-induced ONFH, with abundant naive T cells but reduced mature CD4+ T cells and CD4+ memory T cells compared to both alcohol-induced ONFH and OA. In addition, compared to alcohol-induced ONFH, steroid-induced ONFH was associated with an increase in exhausted/dysfunctional CD8+ T cells which suggests an impaired response to stress and reflects chronic immune dysfunction. Within stromal cell populations, steroid-induced ONFH demonstrated an increase in pericytes, endothelial cells, and mesenchymal cell with osteogenic features as compared to both alcohol-induced ONFH or OA. These findings collectively reveal novel cellular mechanisms underlying steroid-induced ONFH which may contribute to further investigation of etiology-specific pathogenesis and treatment strategies.

title: Cross-species epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity: Insights from Jonathan the Giant Tortoise and human centenarians
authors: Pischedda, S., Gomez Carballa, A., Martinon-Torres, F., Salas, A.
abstract: Can epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity transcend species boundaries? By comparing findings from a previously published epigenomic study of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise, based on buccal scrape and saliva samples, with the analyses of publicly available DNA methylation data from exceptionally long-lived humans based on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), this comparative study reveals intriguing molecular parallels across evolutionarily distant species. Human individuals aged 110+ years exhibited significantly higher global methylation entropy than those aged 60-82 years. Furthermore, 12 candidate genes displayed a distinctive promoter methylation entropy profile, with lower values at the youngest and oldest ages than in intermediate-age groups. Strikingly, these genes were enriched in telomere-related biological processes, highlighting a compelling link between epigenomic patterns and pathways implicated in aging. The correspondence between the findings in humans and previously reported observations in Jonathan suggests testable hypotheses about epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity that may be conserved across species and extend beyond tissue-specific effects.

title: GPBench: A benchmark framework for genomic prediction
authors: Zhang, X., Luo, H., Li, G., Zhang, X., Wang, S., Liu, L., Guo, M., Tan, Q., Domeniconi, C., Chen, J., Wang, J., Yu, G.
abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) has emerged as a powerful data mining strategy for disease risk assessment and molecular breeding. GP leverages genome-wide genetic variations and phenotypic information through a computational model to estimate genetic potential or disease risk. However, the field of GP still faces several major challenges: (i) dataset bias and insufficient representativeness; (ii) the lack of standardized evaluation protocols and a systematic benchmarking framework; (iii) heavy reliance on empirical expertise for experimental result interpretation, which hinders large-scale and systematic analysis. These issues make it difficult to conduct systematic cross-species evaluation and comparison of GP methods, and their authentic applications. To address these challenges, we established a standardized and extensible GP benchmark framework-GPBench. We first collected and harmonized public datasets from 16 species, covering animals, plants, and microorganisms, comprising 57 traits, 40,821 samples, and 493,821 single-nucleotide polymorphisms. Then, using the standardized datasets, the framework evaluates 21 GP models and provides a unified assessment across four dimensions: effectiveness, sensitivity, robustness, and scalability. Furthermore, we developed a large language model-based intelligent analysis system to facilitate the interpretation of GP experiments and model recommendations. GPBench provides the community with a fair, unified, and scalable platform (https://www.sdu-idea.cn/GPBench/) and an open-source library for comparing and optimizing GP methods, ultimately accelerating the application of GP in life sciences and biomedical research.

title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence
authors: Wang, R., Jin, J., Pott, S., Zhou, J.
abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We used this framework to train Mola, a model of single-molecule chromatin accessibility. We harness Mola to investigate sequence-based regulatory code and mechanisms for multiple aspects of chromatin regulation at the single-molecule level. By quantifying sequence-driven nucleosome regulation, we reveal distinct modes of transcription factor engagement with nucleosomes, including a novel nucleosome-trapping factor, ZNF146. We characterized the sequence determinants governing the +1 nucleosome after transcription start sites and identified YY1 as the strongest +1 nucleosome-positioning factor. Leveraging long-context single-molecule modeling, we further discovered a shared sequence basis for the co-accessibility of regulatory elements and the co-footprinting of transcription factors. Joint prediction of DNA methylation and accessibility reveals a sequence-driven bimodal state mediated by methylation-sensitive transcription factors. Beyond static single-molecule snapshots, the S2d framework can generate pseudo-dynamic trajectories of chromatin states and propose a roadmap toward genome-wide chromatin dynamics. Moreover, we showed that Mola can predict and interpret the effects of genetic variants at the single-molecule level, revealing how sequence changes reshape distal regulatory coordination. Together, this sequence-to-distribution framework lays the foundation for understanding how genomic sequence encodes stochastic and dynamic genome regulation, and how genetic variation changes it, one molecule at a time.

title: Differential Gene Expression and Functional Enrichment Analysis of Breast Tumor and Normal Tissue RNA-seq Data: A Reanalysis of GEO Dataset GSE210787
abstract: Background: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) allows a global assessment of expression differences between biological states. The present study reanalyzed publicly available RNA-seq data from human breast tumors and normal tissues to identify DEGs and to investigate functional enrichment. Methods: Twelve paired-end RNA-seq samples from the GEO series GSE210787 were analyzed, including six tumor and six normal samples. Reads were obtained using the SRA Toolkit, checked with FastQC and MultiQC, trimmed with fastp, aligned to the GRCh38.p14 reference with STAR, and quantified at the gene level with featureCounts. Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2 in the Galaxy environment. The project report details criteria of adjusted p-value < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change [≥] 1. Gene Ontology enrichment was performed using g:Profiler and KEGG overrepresentation analysis was performed separately for the up- and down-regulated gene sets. Results: The project report contains a list of 120 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 69 upregulated and 51 downregulated genes in tumor tissue compared with normal tissue. One upregulated-gene GO Cellular Component term, cell periphery (GO:0071944), was observed with a P-value of approximately 0.017585 and 29 overlapping genes. The original report does not specify if this P-value is nominal or adjusted. No significant GO terms were found for the down-regulated gene set. After multiple testing corrections, no KEGG pathway was significant; the lowest adjusted p-value for the upregulated group was about 0.71393. Conclusion: The project identified differences in expression between tumor and normal samples, but no KEGG pathway reached the set FDR significance threshold. The final interpretation needs to check sample metadata, DESeq2 contrast, GO significance statistic, KEGG background universe and analytical parameters against the original results. Keywords: RNA-seq; breast tumor; differential expression; DESeq2; Gene Ontology; KEGG pathway; transcriptomics; cell periphery.

title: NeuroWeave-3D: Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Completion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities
abstract: Multi-parametric MRI segmentation models are accurate when all prescribed sequences are available but can be brittle under missing or corrupted modalities. We propose NeuroWeave-3D, a 3D glioma segmentation framework that treats missing modalities as uncertain evidence rather than deterministic channels to reconstruct. The model combines spatial modality routing, probabilistic latent feature completion, complete-to-missing consistency, and voxel-level uncertainty estimation. A curriculum over all non-empty MRI modality subsets trains one network for arbitrary sequence availability. We define a BraTS-centered evaluation that reports complete-input accuracy, macro and worst-case missing-modality performance, corruption robustness, calibration, and failure detection.

title: High-throughput sequencing of unmethylated DNA (UMR-seq) reveals extensive epigenetic variation in the hypomethylome of diverse plant species
authors: Putland, V., Robinson, H., Eglitis-Sexton, J. I. M., Yoshikawa, G. V., Hintzsche, J., Andrews, H., Andersen, S., Yoon, S., Tong, J., Mangila, L. M., Sree, A., Zanini, S., Schmidt, M., Zhang, Y., Snowdon, R. J., Golicz, A., Voss-Fels, K. P., Hickey, L. T., Crisp, P. A.
abstract: The unmethylated regions (UMRs) in a genome can reveal the location of genes and gene regulatory loci. However, discovering UMR variation across and between entire genomes and disentangling the contribution of genetics and epigenetics to traits are challenging because they require separate and costly whole-DNA methylome and whole-genome genetic analyses. In many species this is prohibitively expensive for even a small number of samples, curtailing analysis on a population or breeding scale. Here we introduce UMR-seq, a method for the specific capture of UMRs from a genome and simultaneous sequencing of genetic variants in a single economical and scalable assay. UMR-seq charts the hypomethylome, revealing that it is highly enriched with functionally important regulatory loci. While UMRs are highly stable between vegetative tissues in plants, we find they are dynamic in the endosperm and vary substantially between accessions. Adaptable to diverse species, using this method we uncover a positive correlation between gene number in a species and UMR content, reflecting gene regulatory space in a genome. At 1/50th of the conventional cost of methylome sequencing in wheat, UMR-seq enables simultaneous population scale analysis of genetic and epigenetic variation in the functional genomic space. We reveal that in a panel of 187 elite wheat cultivars, profiling UMR variation improved genomic prediction across population groups, and UMR-based association mapping identified trait associations that were largely distinct from those detected with SNPs, providing new opportunities to understand trait biology and to enhance predictive breeding.

title: Shapley fields reveal mosaic chemotopic organization in the mouse Olfactory bulb across diverse chemical feature sets
abstract:
by Nikola Milićević, Shawn D. Burton, Matt Wachowiak, Vladimir Itskov 

Neural representations in the olfactory bulb (OB) remain poorly understood compared to well-established coding principles in other sensory systems. This difficulty arises because a natural coordinate system for olfactory stimulus space has not yet been identified, complicating the characterization of neural receptive fields analogous to those in other sensory modalities. Moreover, the extent to which these tuning properties are spatially organized within the OB remains unclear. To advance our understanding of the olfactory coding, we introduce an interpretable method of Shapley fields, as an olfactory analog of retinotopic receptive fields. Shapley fields are spatial distributions of chemical feature importance for the tuning of OB glomeruli. We used this tool to investigate chemotopy in the OB with diverse sets of chemical features using widefield epifluorescence recordings of the mouse dorsal OB in response to stimuli across a wide range of the chemical space. We found that Shapley fields reveal a weak chemotopic organization of the chemical feature sensitivity of dorsal OB glomeruli. This organization was consistent across animals and mostly agreed across very different chemical feature sets: (i) the expert-curated PubChem database features and (ii) features derived from a Graph Neural Network trained on human olfactory perceptual tasks. This chemotopy involved at least three chemical feature dimensions, rather than one or two dominant properties. Moreover, we found that the principal components of the Shapley fields corresponded to single commonly accepted chemical classification groups. This implies that these chemical groups could have been identified purely from the mouse olfactory responses. Our findings suggest that Shapley fields may serve as a chemical feature-agnostic method for investigating olfactory perception.

title: Bayesian efficient coding
abstract:
by Il Memming Park, Jonathan W. Pillow 

The efficient coding hypothesis, which proposes that neurons are optimized to maximize information about the environment, has provided a guiding theoretical framework for sensory and systems neuroscience. More recently, a theory known as the Bayesian Brain hypothesis has focused on the brain’s ability to integrate sensory and prior sources of information in order to perform Bayesian inference. Although pieces of a connection between these two hypotheses have appeared in prior work, a general formulation that treats the optimality criterion as an arbitrary functional of the posterior distribution – and thereby admits both information-based and other objectives within a single framework – has remained largely implicit. Here we make this formulation explicit, developing a Bayesian theory of efficient coding that defines Bayesian efficient codes in terms of four basic ingredients: (1) a stimulus prior distribution; (2) an encoding model; (3) a capacity constraint, specifying a neural resource limit; and (4) a loss functional, quantifying the desirability or undesirability of various posterior distributions. Classic efficient codes arise as the special case in which the loss functional is the posterior entropy, leading to a code that maximizes mutual information, but alternate loss functionals give solutions that differ dramatically from information-maximizing codes. Within this framework we introduce  covtropy , a novel family of losses defined on posterior distributions and parameterized by a single exponent, and use it to show that decorrelation of sensory inputs – optimal under classic efficient codes in low-noise settings – can be disadvantageous for objectives that penalize large errors. We then reanalyze Laughlin’s seminal data on contrast coding in the blowfly large monopolar cell, and find that the measured response nonlinearity is better explained by minimizing Lp reconstruction error with  p  = 1/2 than by information maximization, overturning a forty-year-old interpretation. Bayesian efficient coding thus enlarges the family of codes that are optimal under different objectives and provides a more general framework for understanding the design principles of sensory systems.

title: MoleMap: fast alignment-free molecule mapping for long-read and linked-read sequencing data
abstract:
Background
                      With sequencing costs continuing to decline, the computational expenses of read alignment in genome analysis are becoming an increasingly important consideration. When only portions of the genome are of interest – as in most clinical genome analyses – or base-pair precise alignment is not required, performing full read alignment on whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data imposes unnecessary computational costs. Alignment provides the base-by-base precision necessar​y to identify variants relative to a reference sequence. To improve efficiency, sequence reads can first be rapidly mapped to approximate chromosomal locations, allowing expensive alignment to be restricted to specified target regions subsequently. This mapping-first approach avoids performing base-pair precise alignment across the entire genome. 
                  
                     Results
                      We introduce  MoleMap , a “molecule mapping” method for long reads and linked-read molecules that pre-filters WGS data for downstream targeted analyses. MoleMap uses a minimized open-addressing  k -mer index of the reference genome and a fast  k -mer clustering procedure to assign reads or molecules to genomic regions. In our evaluation, MoleMap identifies the correct mapping location for a comparable number of reads as other mapping and standard alignment tools on simulated data and achieves high agreement with other tools on real data while running 3 − 8 × faster than other mappers and 10 − 60 × faster than full aligners on 32 threads. In addition, its low memory footprint allows whole-genome processing on a standard laptop computer. As proofs of concept, we use MoleMap to filter reads for local assembly of a known variant region that involves non-reference sequence and showcase its use in diagnosing a patient with a rare disease. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      MoleMap is a practical mapping tool for whole-genome data that accelerates targeted analyses by selecting reads from loci of interest before costly alignment. By identifying locus-specific reads, it decreases the volume of data passed to downstream processing steps. In a clinical sequencing setting, this can substantially reduce computational costs and diagnostic turnaround times.

title: GmRVE8a, a circadian clock‐associated gene, negatively regulates flowering and maturity in soybean
authors:
Shibo Sun, 
Maoxiang Yang, 
Tingting Wu, 
Bingjun Jiang, 
Xuegang Sun, 
Hongchang Jia, 
Xiangyu Yao, 
Yanhui Sun, 
Qimeng Li, 
Peiguo Wang, 
Liwei Jiang, 
Chao Qin, 
Shan Yuan, 
Zhaoming Qi, 
Shi Sun, 
Huihui Li, 
Tianfu Han, 
Baiquan Sun
abstract:
Significance Statement 
 Flowering time and maturity determine where soybean can be grown and how reliably it produces yield. By integrating population genomics, deep learning, and functional validation, this study reveals  GmRVE8a  as a circadian clock-associated regulator of soybean developmental timing, advancing our understanding of photoperiodic adaptation and providing a candidate target for crop improvement.
 
 
 SUMMARY 
 Precise regulation of flowering time and maturity is critical for achieving high and stable soybean yields, and the circadian clock plays a central role in coordinating these developmental transitions. Soybean is a typical short-day crop with a pronounced photoperiodic response; however, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian regulation to photoperiod-dependent flowering and maturity remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated genome-wide association analysis with deep learning approaches using 257 soybean germplasm accessions spanning 14 maturity groups and identified  GmRVE8a , a homolog of the Arabidopsis circadian clock gene  REVEILLE , as a strong candidate locus associated with soybean maturity across two field environments. Haplotype analysis demonstrated that accessions carrying the  GmRVE8a 
 
    H1 
  haplotype consistently flowered and matured significantly later than those carrying  GmRVE8a 
 
    H2 
 . Functional validation revealed that knockout of  GmRVE8a  markedly accelerated flowering and maturity, whereas overexpression of  GmRVE8a  significantly delayed both processes. qRT-PCR assays further suggested that  GmRVE8a  may repress flowering and delay maturity by promoting the expression of  GmFT4 , a flowering-inhibitory member of the  FT  family, and is unlikely to act by directly regulating  E1  expression. Collectively, our findings suggest  GmRVE8a  as a circadian clock-associated negative regulator of soybean flowering and maturity, and highlight it as a promising candidate for molecular breeding aimed at improving adaptation to diverse photoperiodic environments.

title: Telomere‐to‐telomere genome assembly of the endangered Jacktree (Sinojackia xylocarpa Hu) reveals its centromeric landscape and evolutionary dilemma as a small population
authors:
Si‐Di Liang, 
Si‐Si Zheng, 
Lei Wu, 
Ang Liu, 
Hong‐Hu Meng, 
Yun Jiang, 
Zheng‐Wei Wang, 
Bin‐Jie Ge, 
Wen‐Li Zou, 
Qian Wan, 
Xi‐Ling Dai, 
Gregor Kozlowski, 
Nai‐Wei Li, 
Xiao‐Ling Yan, 
Yi‐Gang Song
abstract:
Significance Statement 
 We report a T2T genome of endangered  Sinojackia xylocarpa , whose centromeres comprise diverse transposable element (TE) families, and identify a centromere-like domain and inversion polymorphisms on the chr1 right arm. Small population genomic erosion weakens purifying selection and creates an evolutionary dilemma, underscoring the T2T genome's value for endangered plant conservation.
 
 Our T2T genome of  Sinojackia xylocarpa  reveals centromeres composed of diverse TEs, with LTR retrotransposons and LINEs as major components. Recombination suppression linked to LTR accumulation and inversions has led to the accumulation of deleterious mutations in populations, particularly in DNA repair genes. This genomic erosion creates an evolutionary dilemma by preventing the purging of deleterious alleles, compromising the long-term adaptability of small populations. 
 
 SUMMARY 
 The endangered status of many plant species is often attributed to a decline in fitness, which drives a sustained decrease in population size under natural conditions. However, the role of highly repetitive genomic regions in the decline of endangered plants remains poorly understood. Here, we present the gap-free telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome for the endangered Jacktree ( Sinojackia xylocarpa  Hu). It has a genome size of 961.94 Mb, an N50 of 78.05 Mb, and 36 446 predicted protein-coding genes. Using CENH3 chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), we identified centromeric regions across all 12 chromosomes and revealed that  S. xylocarpa  centromeres are composed of diverse transposable element (TE) families, with long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposons and LINE elements as major components. Notably, the right arm of chromosome 1 exhibited ectopic CENH3 enrichment and a TE accumulation similar to that of centromeric regions, suggesting the formation of a centromere-like chromatin domain. In addition, we detected inversion polymorphisms and inversion heterozygotes in natural populations, predominantly concentrated on the same chromosomal arm. These features may be associated with meiotic abnormalities. Using a high-quality T2T genome assembly, we identified a pattern of genomic erosion facing these small populations characterized by local suppression of recombination linked LTR proliferation and by the accumulation of deleterious mutations in DNA repair genes. This genomic erosion creates an evolutionary dilemma that impairs the purging of deleterious alleles, ultimately threatening long-term adaptability and survival. This study highlights the utility of T2T genome assembly for the conservation of endangered plants.

abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 Maize production is influenced by both macronutrient-driven growth and resistance to various abiotic and biotic stresses. While phosphorus (P) is essential for maize growth and productivity, its role in maize immunity remains elusive. Here, we characterized a maize lesion mimic mutant,  les33,  which exhibits enhanced resistance to southern corn rust (SCR) and  Curvularia  leaf spot (CLS). Positional cloning indicated that  ZmPHO2 , encoding an E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme involved in P homeostasis, was the causal gene. In  les33 , increased P level was accompanied by upregulated defence-related gene expression and elevated accumulation of phenylalanine-derived salicylic acid, lignin, and flavonoids, establishing a genetic link between P status and immune activation. Consistently, exogenous phosphate (Pi) application activates defence-related gene expression and enhances resistance to SCR and CLS in a hydroponics system. In particular, flg22-triggered defence marker gene expression, phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and burst of reactive oxygen species (ROS) were enhanced by Pi application, indicating a positive role of P in potentiating PAMP-triggered immunity (PTI). Moreover, field trials showed that application of Pi fertilizer improved SCR resistance in a Pi-dose-dependent manner, further supporting a critical role of P in maize immunity. Taken together, this study provides both genetic and agronomic evidence that P primes defence responses, and highlights optimized Pi fertilization as a practical strategy to coordinate growth and immunity in maize production.

title: Soil engineering by an invasive ant reprograms plant growth–defense trade‐offs to entrench a tripartite mutualism
authors:

abstract:
Schematic diagram illustrating the associations between ant nesting and the ant–aphid mutualism.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Ants are ubiquitous ecosystem engineers, yet the mechanisms through which their nesting activity regulates mutualistic interactions remain elusive.
Here, we provide evidence consistent with the hypothesis that ant nesting initiates a soil–plant–herbivore cascade that reinforces a tripartite mutualism. Using the invasive fire ant  Solenopsis invicta  as a model system in both laboratory and field settings, we show that ant nesting increases soil nitrate and ammonium concentrations, which are associated with enhanced plant growth. These nesting-related changes coincide with shifts in the host plant's hormonal signaling network: auxin signaling is systemically elevated, whereas salicylic acid defense pathways and jasmonate signal transduction are suppressed.
Plants associated with ant nests exhibit compromised defense responses to aphid herbivory. This shift toward a growth-biased physiology supports larger aphid populations, which in turn provide increased carbohydrate rewards for ants, augmenting ant colony survival and brood biomass.
Collectively, our findings suggest a potential terrestrial feedback loop in which ants indirectly enhance their own performance through nesting-associated changes in soil nutrients and plant physiology, which ultimately benefit a mutualist herbivore. In doing so, this study establishes a tripartite ant–plant–herbivore mutualism that extends beyond the ‘food-for-protection’ paradigm as classically defined.

title: Fast and accurate resolution of ecDNA sequence using Cycle-Extractor
abstract: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) plays a key role in cancer pathology. ecDNAs mediate high oncogene amplification and expression and are associated with worse patient outcomes. Accurately determining the structure of these circular molecules is essential for understanding their function, yet reconstructing ecDNA cycles from sequencing data remains challenging. We introduce Cycle-Extractor (CE) for this task. CE takes as input a breakpoint graph derived from either short or long read sequencing data and extracts cycles of maximum length-weighted copy number. CE utilizes a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and a separate traversal procedure, enabling fast optimization and compatibility with open-source ILP solvers. We evaluated CE against CoRAL (long-read, mixed-integer quadratically constrained programming), Decoil (long-reads), and AmpliconArchitect (AA; short reads) on both simulated data and real cancer cell lines. On simulated ecDNA, CE achieves accuracy comparable to CoRAL across three metrics and consistently outperforms AA and Decoil. On cancer cell lines, CE produces longer and heavier cycles than AA, and performs comparably to CoRAL, while being on average 40× faster. These results demonstrate that CE accurately reconstructs ecDNA from both short and long-read sequencing data, and that long-read inputs allow CE to recover more complete, higher-confidence ecDNA structures. CE improved the prediction of many ecDNA structures. On PC3 ecDNA containing MYC, CE uses ONT data to reconstruct a substantially larger and higher-copy sequence (4.2 Mbp) compared to the short-read-derived reconstruction (690 kbp). CRISPR-CATCH experiments confirm the presence of a large ecDNA molecule, validating the long-read-based CE reconstruction.

title: Tissue-specific accumulation of Na+ in leaves of 2 tomato species is linked to differences in symplastic transport
abstract: Abstract Soil salinization is a growing global threat that limits crop productivity. To cope with sodium (Na + ) stress, plants have evolved tolerance mechanisms, including excluding Na +  from shoot tissues and tolerating elevated Na +  within shoots through tissue- and cellular-level mechanisms. Most current knowledge of Na +  accumulation comes from organ- or whole-plant measurements that lack the spatial resolution needed to resolve cellular tolerance mechanisms. Here, we used histological approaches to map leaf Na +  distribution in tomato ( Solanum ) species with contrasting salt-tolerance strategies. In the moderately salt-tolerant, Na + -excluding domesticated tomato (cv. M82), Na +  was largely confined to the bundle sheath, whereas in salt-tolerant, Na + -including wild relatives, Na +  accumulated throughout the blade mesophyll. Consistent with these cell population-specific Na +  patterns, M82, but not  Solanum pennellii , exhibited reduced symplastic transport and plasmodesma permeability under salt stress. A genetic screen combined with transcriptome profiling implicated  Plasmodesmata-Located Protein 1  ( PDLP1 ), a regulator of callose-mediated plasmodesma closure, in establishing symplastic domains in M82 that restrict Na +  movement into the mesophyll. Moreover,  PDLP1  expression was negatively correlated with mesophyll Na +  levels across wild and domesticated tomatoes. Collectively, these results link cellular Na +  enrichment patterns to symplastic connectivity and suggest that  PDLP1 -mediated regulation of plasmodesmata contributes to leaf-level salt-tolerance strategies.

title: Maternal genomic legacy of Altaic-speaking populations reveals broad Eurasian maternal lineage diversity with a northern East Asian connection
abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), inherited maternally and without recombination, is crucial for tracing maternal lineages and studying population history. Although Altaic-speaking groups are widespread across Eurasia, their maternal genetic data remain limited. Here, we assembled a comparative dataset of 58,257 modern and 7,425 ancient individuals, including high-quality mtDNA single-nucleotide polymorphism variation data from large-scale array studies of representative Altaic individuals. This dataset enabled a detailed assessment of maternal genetic diversity and geographic structure in Altaic-speaking populations. Our results reveal diverse patterns of maternal haplogroup composition among Altaic-speaking populations, including lineages whose distributions align with enrichment in ancient mtDNA datasets from archaeological contexts associated with subsistence strategies such as hunter-gathering, pastoralism, and farming across northern East Asia, Siberia, and western Eurasia. Manchu and Mongolian populations show stronger maternal affinity with northern East Asians, whereas Kazakhs carry higher proportions of western and northern Eurasian lineages. Manchu populations show some north–south differentiation across different geographic grouping schemes. This study expands mtDNA resources for underrepresented Altaic-speaking populations and improves understanding of their maternal genetic diversity.

title: VENAS2: Bidirectional Mutation Modeling for Genomic Surveillance Reveals Reversions and Hidden Transmission Links in Pathogens
abstract: Abstract Accurately resolving pathogen evolution is essential for genomic surveillance, yet existing approaches often assume unidirectional mutation accumulation and fail to capture reversions that obscure lineage classification and transmission dynamics. Here we present VENAS2, a scalable framework that integrates genomic, temporal and geographic information to construct spatiotemporal evolutionary networks while explicitly modeling bidirectional mutational processes. Applied to 7.25 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes from GISAID between December 2019 and June 2024, VENAS2 reconstructed the evolutionary history of SARS-CoV-2 and precisely inferred the temporal dynamics of major variants of concern. Further application to the Viridian dataset revealed 4,654 distinct genomic sites with at least one potential reversion event, providing a systematic view of potential reversion signals during viral evolution. Extending to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, VENAS2 delineated major lineages and identified over threefold additional transmission clusters beyond conventional genomic distance-based methods, uncovering hidden links enriched for drug-resistant strains. These results demonstrate VENAS2’s capacity to uncover cryptic evolutionary processes across viruses and bacteria, providing a generalizable platform that bridges genomic surveillance with actionable public health response.

title: Learning Constraints in Protein Evolution beyond Known Substitution Frequencies
abstract: Abstract During the evolution of protein sequences, amino acid substitutions follow broad patterns that are well established, such as those induced by the physico-chemical properties of residues or the position of sites along the sequence. While these deviations from random changes have been exploited for practical applications, such as to simulate protein evolution or to score protein alignments, they are too general to predict the precise evolution of individual protein sequences. To investigate whether protein sequences contain contextual information about their subsequent evolution beyond that captured by conventional substitution statistics and evolutionary conservation, we trained deep learning models based on an Evolutionary Scale Modelling (ESM2) encoder to predict the rate, the position and the nature of the amino-acid substitutions in the evolution of ancestral sequences and compared their performance to simpler and explainable heuristics.Our results show that predicting the rate of amino acid changes is achieved equally well by deep learning and by using evolutionary information in outgroup sequences. This suggests that the protein sequence does not contain information that significantly improves the predictions for this task. On the opposite, we show that deep learning models predict the position of these substitutions more accurately than statistics-based baselines. Predictions of the nature of substitutions largely outperform baselines, with over 37% accuracy overall. We observe that rapidly evolving sequences are harder to predict and substitutions preferentially occur between chemically similar amino acids. Interestingly, predictive information is predominantly contained within a local sequence context of 16 residues. These findings indicate that the nature of substitutions in protein evolution is partly governed by predictive rules that remain to be discovered through a more accurate modelling that could describe evolutionary trajectories based on sequence context alone.

title: Differential selection between sexes and the evolution of recombination in haplodiploids
abstract: Abstract Eusocial Hymenoptera present the highest known recombination rates among metazoans, which evolved several times independently among bees, ants and wasps. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this observation, including stronger selection for recombination caused by coevolving parasites and pathogens, and strong sexual selection among haploid males due to male-biased sex ratios among reproductive individuals. In this article, we explore the effects of haplodiploidy and differential selection between sexes on the evolution of recombination, by analyzing a three-locus model in which selection for recombination stems from negative epistasis between selected loci. Our analytical predictions are compared with the results of individual-based simulations in which deleterious mutations occur along a linear chromosome. Our results show that, at mutation-selection balance for deleterious alleles, increasing the strength of selection against deleterious alleles (due to the effect of male haploidy and/or sexual selection) tends to reduce selection for recombination. However, an increase in the overall magnitude of negative epistasis (which may also be due to male haploidy and/or sexual selection) combined with the fact that recombination only occurs in females may increase selection for recombination substantially. Our model also shows that, in conditions favoring recombination, increasing recombination in meioses leading to parthenogenetic ovules (and male offspring) may yield stronger benefits than in meioses leading to fertilized ovules (and female offspring).

title: NLP-12/Cholecystokinin signaling stabilizes sensory dendritic structure and protects neuronal healthspan in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Abstract Aging selectively degrades neuronal structure and function, yet the signals that actively preserve neuronal integrity over adult life remain incompletely defined. In  Caenorhabditis elegans , the PVD sensory neuron develops progressive excessive higher-order dendritic branching during normal aging that correlates with declines in proprioceptive locomotion. Using this system as a quantitative  in vivo  readout of neuronal healthspan, we identify the cholecystokinin-like neuropeptide NLP-12 as a protective signal that preserves PVD homeostasis across adulthood.  nlp-12  loss-of-function animals show early-onset excessive branching and earlier declines in proprioceptive function, whereas  nlp-12  overexpression attenuates excessive branching in aged adults without extending lifespan, indicating a neuron-focused effect on healthspan. Longitudinal analysis of an NLP-12::mKate reporter reveals age-related reduction in extracellular delivery of NLP-12 and increased retention in the soma of the DVA interneuron, where  nlp-12  is predominantly expressed. Consistent with a requirement for secretory trafficking, disrupting the NLP-12 signal peptide abolishes the rescue effects of wild-type  nlp-12  reintroduction in  nlp-12  mutants. Additionally, chemogenetic silencing of DVA during adulthood similarly accelerates excessive PVD branching, supporting an ongoing requirement for secreted DVA-derived NLP-12. Receptor genetics further show that both cholecystokinin receptor homologs, CKR-1 and CKR-2, are required downstream of NLP-12-mediated neuroprotection during aging. Finally, human cholecystokinin rescues PVD branching and partially improves proprioceptive patterning in  nlp-12  mutants, supporting functional conservation. Together, these findings define conserved cholecystokinin-like neuropeptide signaling as an adult maintenance mechanism that buffers age-associated decline in neuronal resilience.

title: Holistic integration of protein interaction datasets establishes a framework for exploring the organization and composition of Caenorhabditis elegans germ granules
abstract: Abstract Spatiotemporal organization of biological molecules is a key driver of cellular processes, including many post-transcriptional epigenetic processes. The germline-specific germ granules are biomolecular condensates that act as hubs for mRNA and small RNA processing and are core regulators of germline gene expression programming. Germ granules have been studied extensively in  Caenorhabditis elegans , and recent developments have led to many subdivisions of the germ granule into specialized compartments. Rapid advancements in microscopy and protein-protein interaction (PPI) screening techniques have produced a large amount of data towards characterizing the localization of proteins to specific granules. However, common methods used to probe PPIs are limited in their ability to robustly detect valid interactions, especially the multivalent and sometimes transient ones observed in granule environments. Here we perform a meta-analysis of granule protein interaction screens. While these experiments generally enrich for proteins matching the profile of granule-associated proteins, we find that when considering screens individually, reproducibility is surprisingly low, highlighting not only the variability inherent in these methods but also the dynamic nature of the PPI networks present in granules. We developed an algorithm to provide a measure of each protein’s association with specific granules across various experiments (a “granule association metric” or GAM). By further clustering and investigation of the GAM matrix, we demonstrate the power of this holistic approach to provide deeper insights into germ granule organization, highlight novel candidates, and act as a resource to inform future investigations into granules and their constituent proteins.

title: Embodied intelligence for crop production
authors: Yubin Zhang, Xiujuan Chai, Tan Sun
abstract: Global agriculture faces growing food demand, labor shortages, and climate uncertainty. Although automation has improved agricultural operations, adapting to variable crop states and unstructured environments remains challenging. Embodied intelligence integrates multimodal perception, contextual reasoning, and adaptive action through continuous interaction with crops and their environment. This review examines advances in embodied perception, decision-making, and execution for crop production. We discuss how multimodal sensing, crop growth models, and adaptive control connect individual operations with management objectives across the crop growth cycle.

title: A systemic auxin state integrates light and temperature to gate lateral rooting in Arabidopsis
authors: Chengzhi Ren, Jule Bodendorf, Aleš Pěnčík, Alberto González-Delgado, Shasha Li, Miguel A. Moreno-Risueno, Krzysztof Wabnik, Ondrej Novak, Jürgen Kleine-Vehn
abstract: Short Summary: Light perceived above ground determines whether root branching continues or is suppressed during warming. These cues systemically shape the availability of the phytohormone auxin throughout the root, creating a shared hormonal environment that gates whether locally specified branching sites develop. Systemic control of auxin breakdown thereby translates environmental conditions across the plant into local decisions on organ formation.

title: Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges
authors: Jiheon Han, Amen Seo, Pham Cong Anh, Trinh Minh Vu, Scott A. Jackson, Ethan Pickering, Kyung Do Kim
abstract: Short summary: Large language models (LLMs) and biological foundation models (Bio-FMs) are increasingly proposed for predictive plant breeding. This review audits what they have demonstrated: direct LLM evidence centers on literature retrieval and evidence organization, Bio-FMs support molecular prediction, and none has yet been validated in breeding programs. A human-supervised agentic framework with output-specific validation is proposed to guide their responsible use.

title: Nonstoichiometric Defect Engineering in Mn2+‐Doped MgGa2O4 Persistent Phosphors Toward Enhanced Luminescence and Multimodal Optical Manometry
authors:
Peng Du, 
Yifei Yu, 
Yue Guo, 
Przemysław Woźny, 
Shualing Ma, 
Laihui Luo, 
Marcin Runowski
abstract:
Mg 2+  deficiency transforms Mn 2+ -doped MgGa 2 O 4  into a multifunctional persistent phosphor, enhancing green emission, thermal stability, and afterglow effect for optical anti-counterfeiting. Under compression, spectral shifts enable visual pressure sensing with a sensitivity of 5.01 nm GPa −1  over a pressure range up to 30 GPa. Defect engineering thus offers a promising route to high-performance optical manometry.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Mn 2+ -doped MgGa 2 O 4  persistent phosphors were synthesized through a nonstoichiometric engineering strategy to precisely regulate their luminescence properties. By introducing Mg 2+  deficiency, the luminescence intensity, thermal stability and persistent luminescence performance are simultaneously enhanced, enabling their potential application in optical anti-counterfeiting. Furthermore, the in situ high-pressure X-ray diffraction measurements demonstrate the excellent structural robustness of the designed phosphors over the investigated pressure range, indicating their suitability for high-pressure manometry. Upon compression, the resultant phosphors exhibit pronounced pressure-induced spectral red-shift, enabling tunable luminescence and visualized pressure sensing. Notably, compared with the stoichiometric counterpart, the Mg 2+ -deficient phosphors display significantly enhanced pressure responsiveness, resulting in improved optical manometric performance with higher sensitivity and an extended working pressure range. Specifically, within a broad pressure range of 0–30 GPa, the Mg 0.939 Ga 2 O 4 :Mn 2+  phosphor achieve pressure sensitivities of 5.01 and 2.29 nm GPa −1  based on the emission band centroid and full width at half maximum, respectively. Additionally, the developed phosphors exhibit good colorimetric pressure sensing capability, reaching a maximum relative sensitivity of 12.71% GPa −1 . These results demonstrate that the optical properties of the Mn 2+ -doped MgGa 2 O 4  phosphors can be effectively modulated through the synergistic regulation of nonstoichiometric engineering and pressure, highlighting their application potential in optical anti-counterfeiting and multimodal manometry.

title: Post‐Synthetic Cerium Modification of Commercial NCM811 for Concurrent Cycling and Safety Upgrading
authors:
Wei‐Wei Wang, 
Da‐Kun Chen, 
Wei Kang, 
Xiao‐Mei Wu, 
Qing Cao, 
Quan‐Fang Wang, 
Si‐Yuan Ma, 
Hai‐Long Wang, 
Jing‐Hua Tian, 
Zhong‐Qun Tian
abstract:
Cerium ion doping and CeO 2  coating work synergistically to reinforce commercial NCM811 cathodes. This strategy stabilizes the lattice and strengthens the interface against degradation and side reactions. The modified cathode shows enhanced rate capability and cycling stability. Notably, suppressed gas release improves safety, making this scalable method a promising route for advanced batteries.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The widespread use of Ni-rich LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2  (NCM811) cathodes in high-energy batteries remains limited by structural degradation, side reactions, and oxygen release, yet most modification strategies prove incompatible with commercial materials. This work presents a facile solid-state method that achieves synergistic cerium ion (Ce 3+ ) doping and CeO 2  coating on commercial NCM811 by mixing with CeO 2  nanoparticles followed by calcination. Structural and morphological analyses confirm Ce incorporation into the near-surface lattice and the formation of a nanoscale CeO 2  layer without disturbing the layered framework. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that the optimal 1 wt.% Ce-modified sample exhibits superior rate capability and long-term stability, retaining 82.04% of its initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C, compared to 74.10% for pristine, owing to suppressed cation mixing, enhanced structural stability, and improved Li +  diffusion kinetics. Crucially, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry shows Ce modification curtails O 2  release and reduces H 2  and CO 2  generation across various rates, effectively mitigating gas evolution associated with safety degradation. Accelerating rate calorimetry further confirms delayed thermal runaway and improved adiabatic stability. Overall, this work establishes a scalable post-treatment route to simultaneously boost the electrochemical performance and safety of commercial nickel-rich cathodes, offering a practical solution for next-generation lithium-ion batteries.

title: Glycerol‐Regulated Cytocompatible, Self‐Healing Gel Electrolyte Stabilizes Zinc Metal Anodes for Quasi‐Solid‐State Aqueous Batteries
authors:
Yuchuan Ren, 
Qian Xue, 
Lihong He, 
Canhuang Li, 
Ruixia Li, 
Xiaoyu Bi, 
Jiali Chai, 
Yapeng Cheng, 
Tiezhu Guo, 
Andreu Cabot
abstract:
A glycerol-regulated PVA/PEG self-healing gel electrolyte reconstructs the hydrogen-bonding and Zn 2 
 +  coordination environments, suppressing water-related parasitic reactions and enabling regulated Zn nucleation and homogeneous deposition. The resulting quasi-solid-state electrolyte combines durable Zn-metal reversibility, self-healing functionality, and cytocompatibility, while supporting reversible Zn–S full-cell operation.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Aqueous zinc batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their practical development is strongly limited by the instability of Zn metal in water-containing electrolytes, which promotes corrosion, parasitic reactions, nonuniform ion transport, and dendritic deposition. Here, we develop a glycerol-regulated cytocompatible, self-healing gel electrolyte (SHGE) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol)/poly(ethylene glycol) matrix. Glycerol reorganizes the hydrogen-bonding environment and reduces polymer crystallinity, thereby decreasing water reactivity while enhancing polymer-chain mobility and ionic transport. The resulting gel also modifies the Zn 2+  coordination environment and promotes more regulated interfacial ion transfer, suppressing Zn corrosion and enabling compact and homogeneous Zn deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable plating/stripping for over 3300 h at 5 mA cm − 
 2  and 5 mAh cm − 
 2 . The SHGE further exhibits low in vitro cytotoxicity toward multiple cell types, together with good flexibility and self-healing capability. As a proof of concept for quasi-solid-state full-cell operation, trace thiourea is introduced to promote sulfur redox conversion in Zn–S cells, enabling reversible cycling with high Coulombic efficiency and durable pouch-cell operation. These results establish a multifunctional gel-electrolyte strategy for stabilizing Zn metal anodes while integrating mechanical adaptability and cytocompatibility in quasi-solid-state aqueous batteries.

title: 18F‐FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
authors:
Yi Liu, 
Jindian Li, 
Xiaoyu Pan, 
Xiaoping Xu, 
Xuan Huang, 
Simin He, 
Jianping Zhang, 
Fei Liu, 
Shaoli Song
abstract:
18 F-FGln PET/CT imaging serves as a marker of Gln uptake in hepatocellular carcinoma. Tumors with high Gln uptake drive Treg-mediated immunosuppression and immune evasion during antitumor immunotherapy. Conversely, tumors with low Gln uptake maintain sufficient Gln in the TME, suppressing Tregs and enabling cytotoxic T cells to inhibit tumor growth under antitumor immunotherapy.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by  18 F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine ( 18 F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that  SLC1A5  expression—which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells—was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high  18 F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated  Slc1a5  expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of  Slc1a5  reduced  18 F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after  Slc1a5  suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by  18 F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with  18 F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that  18 F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

title: Combinatorial Tuning of Multigene Biosynthetic Pathways based on RNA Interference
authors:
Zixu Zhang, 
Yingshuang Xu, 
Zijia Li, 
Fei Du, 
Wang Ma, 
Guang Yang, 
Xiaoman Sun
abstract:
Small RNA sequencing identifies candidate endogenous Pol III promoters, and subsequent fluorescence screening measures knockdown efficiency to assess promoter strength. Combining promoter strength and shRNA target position enables fine-grained RNAi regulation of multigene pathways. This strategy enhances β-carotene production in  Schizochytrium  sp. and DHA production in  Yarrowia lipolytica , while bypass pathway screening and tuning improve the DHA/DPA ratio in  Schizochytrium  sp.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Fine-tuning the expression level of multigene pathways remains a major challenge in engineering eukaryotic microbial cell factories. Modifications to individual pathway genes and CRISPR-based approaches often require repeated genome reconstruction, large regulatory components, or complex guide-array assembly. Here, we developed a lightweight, post-transcriptional RNAi-based strategy that enables fine-tuning gene expression without iterative genome editing. Size-selected small-RNA sequencing and functional testing were used to identify endogenous Pol III promoters spanning graded transcriptional strengths in  Schizochytrium  sp. Combining promoter strength with multiple short hairpin RNA (shRNA) target positions expanded the accessible repression range and enabled high-resolution gene-dosage tuning. The RNAi-based combined regulation strategy was applied to the three-gene carotenoid pathway of  Schizochytrium  sp. and the nine-gene docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) pathway of  Yarrowia lipolytica , significantly enhancing the product production in both hosts. Integration of RNAi screening and dosage optimization further identified and tuned bypass pathways, increasing the ratio of DHA to docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) by 4.50-fold versus wild type. These gains were maintained during 5-L fermentation and serial passaging. This work establishes a compact and scalable regulatory framework for engineering complex biosynthetic pathways in eukaryotic microbial hosts.

title: SUMOylated DDX3 Promotes HBV Replication and Tumor Growth of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TRIM28‐DDX3‐KLF4α Signaling Axis
authors:
Yanfang Yang, 
Ting Kong, 
Binghan Wang, 
Xiaoli Jin, 
Lan Huang, 
Nan Zhang, 
Siyu Tang, 
Samina Ejaz Syed, 
Shufang Liang
abstract:
TRIM28 binds to DDX3 protein to catalyze the SUMOylation of DDX3 (S-DDX3), thus the S-DDX3 involves in aberrant alternative splicing of  KLF4  mRNA, and the splicing variant  KLF 4α-mediated cell cycle and signal transduction, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 protein, which promotes progression of HBV-HCC. Conversely, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation that is essential for inhibiting HBV gene transcription and HBsAg secretion.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 DDX3 has dual biological functions of regulating cell proliferation and antiviral effects. Herein, we focus on SUMOylation-mediated DDX3 in the interplay from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) progression. We identified dynamic regulation of SUMOylation and DeSUMOylation of DDX3 at four key lysine (K) residues (K81/K208/K215/K564) in response to HBV infection. During the early stage of HBV acute infection, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation for inhibiting HBV replication. During persistent HBV replication, as SENP1 downregulation and HBV polymerase accumulation, DDX3 disassociates with SENP1 to bind with TRIM28, which induces DDX3 SUMOylation. Meanwhile, SUMOylated DDX3 enhances alternative splicing of  KLF4  mRNAs to generate KLF4α isoform that involves in Cyclin D1-mediated cell cycle progression, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 and promotes HBV-HCC. Moreover, DDX3 expression is positively correlated with  KLF4  mRNA, and high DDX3 level with low TRIM28 expression indicates a better overall survival for HBV-HCC patients. Our findings reveal the dynamic regulation between SUMOylation and deSUMOylation of DDX3, including mediating HBV gene transcription, virus antigen secretion, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, the TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4 axis as a novel therapeutic target for HBV-HCC, exhibiting the dual ability to inhibit tumor progression and disrupt the HBV–host interaction.

title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox via Li Dopants Into P2‐Type Cathodes for High‐Voltage Sodium‐Ion Batteries
authors:
Peng Dai, 
Yanfen Wen, 
Chenguang Shi, 
Jie Fu, 
Jinxia Lin, 
Hang Li, 
Sylvio Indris, 
Jingjing Fan, 
Yuxiang Xie, 
Yonglin Tang, 
Shishi Liu, 
Chenxu Luo, 
Yuan Chen, 
Mohsen Shakouri, 
Tom Regier, 
Fang Fu, 
Jun‐Tao Li, 
Ling Huang, 
Shi‐Gang Sun, 
Ya‐Ping Deng
abstract:
Regulating anionic redox of layered cathodes provides the promises as performance promotor for sodium ion batteries. In this work, Li doping strategy has been developed to stabilize oxygen redox in the voltage window from 4.1 to 4.3 V. The underlying mechanism has been investigated through integrating a variety of characterizations.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Anionic redox offers a pathway to increase the energy density of layered cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet it is often accompanied by structure and interface degradation. Here, we demonstrate that Li dopants as regulators for oxygen redox in P2-Na 0.67 Ni 0.33 Mn 0.67 O 2  through tuning local coordination environments and charge compensation pathways. Li dopants enhance Ni redox activity while moderating transition metal-oxygen (TM-O) coupling at high voltages. The online electrochemical mass spectrometry with  18 O isotope labeling reveals that it suppresses the lattice oxygen participation in electrolyte decomposition and mitigates irreversible oxygen loss. As a result, the Li-doped Na 0.67 Li 0.2 Ni 0.23 Mn 0.67 O 2  exhibits improved rate capability cycling stability, delivering an initial capacity of 116.6 mAh/g with 80% retention after 400 cycles at 1 C, compared to 27% for the undoped counterpart. This work highlights the importance of controlling reactive oxygen species and establishes a strategy to stabilize high-voltage operation by decoupling oxygen redox from degradation pathways in sodium-ion cathodes.

title: Lactylation of HSC70 Impairs Chaperone‐Mediated Autophagy to Promote Pyrin Inflammasome‐Dependent PANoptosis in Macrophages During Sepsis
authors:
Ying Chen, 
Yan Zhang, 
Pei Wang, 
Jiamin Ma, 
Xinru Zhao, 
Yi Li, 
Zhenghao Deng, 
Xueqing Meng, 
Jiali Zhu, 
Liangfang Yao, 
Jinbao Li
abstract:
In sepsis, lactate accumulation drives HSC70 K561 lactylation, which impairs chaperone‐mediated autophagy and blocks CUX1 degradation. Accumulated CUX1 transcriptionally upregulates Pyrin, triggering PANoptosis in macrophages and exacerbating inflammatory storm and organ injury. Targeting lactate production or activating CMA relieves this pathological cascade, providing potential therapeutic strategies for sepsis.








ABSTRACT
Sepsis‐related cytokine storm is associated with poor prognosis in septic patients. IFNγ/LPS can synergistically trigger a sepsis‐associated proinflammatory cytokine storm and induce macrophage death in the form of PANoptosis. The ensuing release of proinflammatory cytokines further amplifies macrophage death, leading to subsequent multiple organ damage. Concurrently, the IFNγ/LPS induced inflammatory cascade also downregulates chaperone‐mediated autophagy (CMA) activity, and this dysregulation further exacerbates the inflammatory response in macrophages and in vivo. Thus, a positive feedback loop between dysfunctional CMA and the inflammatory cascade is established. Enhancing CMA activation reduces macrophage death and organ damage, whereas inhibiting CMA exacerbates macrophage PANoptosis and organ injury. Mechanistically, impaired CMA leads to accumulation of the transcription factor CUX1, which subsequently upregulates Pyrin expression and promotes Pyrin‐mediated PANoptosome assembly, thereby driving macrophage PANoptosis. In addition to the cytokine storm, the lacylation at lysine 561 (K561) of HSC70, a core component of the CMA machinery, is associated with reduced CMA activity. Blocking lactylation can similarly attenuate macrophage death and multiple organ injury in sepsis. Taken together, this “Kla‐CMA‐CUX1/Pyrin‐PANoptosis” signaling axis, linking metabolic reprogramming to immune dysregulation in sepsis, suggests that targeting key nodes of this axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to reduce sepsis‐associated mortality.

title: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
authors:

abstract:
This study demonstrates a vertically aligned CNT (VACNT)‐based heat sink. The nanoporous structure of the VACNT provides a large surface area for convective and radiative exchange, alongside axial conduction, enabling multimodal heat dissipation. Mounted on a CPU, the VACNT with a fin array pattern achieves a steady‐state temperature 6.7°C lower than a conventional aluminum heat sink.








ABSTRACT
A vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)‐based heat sink is demonstrated for passive multimodal thermal management applicable for electronic and semiconductor devices. The VACNT enables multimodal heat dissipation through axial conduction, convection facilitated by its nanoporous morphology, and radiation enabled by its superior emissivity. While conventional metallic heat sinks suffer from low surface emissivity and require complex post‐processing to enhance radiative cooling, the proposed VACNT overcomes these limitations by providing an inherent multiscale structural hierarchy without secondary surface treatments. The thermal conductivity of the freestanding VACNT (500 to 1500 µm heights) is characterized using laser flash analysis and differential scanning calorimetry as 32 to 40 W/mK. Evaluated on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W platform, the 1500 µm‐high VACNT heat sink decreases the peak CPU temperature by 10.7°C compared with a bare CPU. The VACNT can be patterned into the topographic architecture to further improve heat dissipation by increasing the surface area, achieving a 6.7°C lower peak CPU temperature than a conventional aluminum heat sink. Cyclic stability test confirms consistent thermal performance over repeated use. The VACNT practically allows various configurational engineering by molding, rolling, scissoring, and tiling, showcasing its versatility for diverse thermal management applications.

title: Accelerating High‐Fidelity Airfoil Design via Physics‐Informed Video Diffusion Model
authors:
Yifeng Ai, 
Yijia Guo, 
Hongfu Zhang, 
Lei Zhou, 
Tiejun Huang, 
Weiqiu Chen, 
Xuhui He, 
Peng Guo, 
C. W. Lim, 
Lei Ma
abstract:
Physics‐informed video diffusion enables rapid inverse aerodynamic design by mapping target lift‐to‐drag response to airfoil geometries and full‐field flow distributions. Trained on 53 400 DNS samples, the model achieves over 90% fidelity with ∼30 s inference, while experimentally realized propeller designs demonstrate a practical pathway from aerodynamic targets to manufacturable structures.








ABSTRACT
Airfoil design remains a challenging multi‐objective optimization problem requiring precise geometric control for optimal aerodynamic performance. Data‐driven inverse design methods mitigate this complexity but often yield non‐physical results when physical constraints are not explicitly incorporated. Here, we construct a high‐fidelity NACA–Nek1000 datasets with 53 400 samples from direct numerical simulations to train a dual physics‐informed video diffusion model (PVDM). The governing equations of incompressible flow are intrinsically coupled with the diffusion learning process, enabling the reconstruction of full‐field velocity and pressure distributions from lift‐to‐drag response sequences. The PVDM achieves accurate low‐Reynolds number airfoil reconstruction and real‐time flow generation within 30 s per case, approximately 600 times faster than conventional simulations, while maintaining over 90% fidelity. The reconstructed airfoils are further modeled as propeller geometries and experimentally validated, which well fit the simulated lift‐to‐drag response, establishing a rapid and generalizable framework for high‐fidelity, physics‐informed inverse aerodynamic design.

title: Device Stochasticity Directly Implements Bayesian Sampling in Spiking Neurons
authors:
Huannan Zheng, 
Jingli Liu, 
Kezhou Yang
abstract:
Brain‐inspired stochastic spiking turns device noise into Bayesian uncertainty for robust, low‐power neuromorphic computing. 








ABSTRACT
Device stochasticity is considered a non‐ideality in neuromorphic hardware, although stochastic neural activity supports probabilistic computation in biological systems. We show that intrinsic stochastic switching of magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) can be mapped to stochastic‐threshold spiking neurons, providing a physical sampling primitive for Bayesian spiking inference. We develop a spiking Bayesian neural network (SBNN) with neuronal threshold distributions learned during training and sampled during inference. We also introduce a rate‐estimation method that propagates firing probabilities rather than explicit spike sequences, achieving up to a 22‐fold speedup over surrogate‐gradient training. Compared with representative Bayesian neural‐network baselines, SBNN achieves favorable accuracy‐calibration trade‐offs, reaching high accuracy across static and event datasets and low negative log likelihood in both MNIST and Fashion‐MNIST. On MNIST, SBNN retains 96.20%$96.20\%$ accuracy under a normalized weight‐noise standard deviation of 0.20 and 81.30%$81.30\%$ under an input‐noise standard deviation of 0.25, compared with 27.42%$27.42\%$ and 70.27%$70.27\%$, respectively, for the spiking neural network (SNN). Hardware‐in‐the‐loop validation using physical MTJ switching for sampling and software for network arithmetic closely matches software inference in spiking behavior and classification performance. This suggests that intrinsic device stochasticity can be transformed from a hardware non‐ideality into a Bayesian computational resource for compact and noise‐tolerant neuromorphic systems.

title: Multicomponent Molecular Editing of Polybutadiene: From Design Space to Battery Function
authors:
Janna Jeschke, 
Oghenegare Emmanuel Eyankware, 
Ioannis Moutsios, 
Loïc Vidal, 
Cyril Vaulot, 
Azra Kocaarslan, 
Angelina Sarapulova, 
Sonia Dsoke, 
Hatice Mutlu
abstract:
Multicomponent molecular editing transforms polybutadiene into an 18-member polymer library with tunable thermal properties, nanoscale organization, and molecular dynamics. Mapping this multidimensional design space reveals distinct molecular input–property relationships and guides the selection of a candidate electrolyte additive for lithium–sulfur batteries, demonstrating how systematic polymer diversification can bridge molecular design and application-oriented materials discovery.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Multicomponent post-polymerization modification (PPM) enables polymer diversification, yet its potential for exploring structure-property-function relationships remains underexplored. Herein, we report an electrophilic multicomponent molecular editing strategy that enables the construction of a polybutadiene-derived molecular design space through systematic variation of cyclic ethers and  N - or  O- nucleophiles. Combining three cyclic ethers with six nucleophiles generated an 18-member library, varying spacer architecture, polarity, and intermolecular interactions ( P1  -  P18 ). Mapping thermal, selected morphological, and molecular mobility properties revealed substantial changes arising from subtle molecular variations. In particular,  P9  was distinguished by its nanoscale organization and proton relaxation behavior, providing insight into the influence of molecular structure on morphology and molecular dynamics. Mapping these complementary property landscapes guided the selection of  P11  for preliminary evaluation as an electrolyte additive for Li–S batteries, based on its balance of functionality and physicochemical properties. Electrochemical testing in a deliberately LiNO 3 -free model electrolyte revealed that  P11  altered sulfur redox behavior and impedance response, increased Coulombic efficiency, and showed more gradual capacity decay relative to the additive-free baseline, albeit with increased polarization and reduced initial capacity. These trade-offs demonstrate library-guided selection without establishing  P11  as an optimized additive. Descriptive sensitivity analysis identified nucleophile identity as the dominant input for functionalization degree (FD) and thermal stability, whereas glass-transition temperature showed sensitivity to both molecular inputs.

title: A Water Compartment Cell Culture Lid Enables Stable Longitudinal Recording of Neuronal Networks In Vitro
authors:
Benedikt Maurer, 
Fabio Fischer, 
Giulia Amos, 
Vaiva Vasiliauskaitė, 
János Vörös
abstract:
A cell culture lid with an integrated water compartment eliminates evaporation from microelectrode arrays while preserving gas exchange. Freed from the osmotic drift and repeated medium exchanges that disturb conventional recordings, patterned human iPSC‐derived neuronal networks are recorded continuously for five weeks. Single‐spike resolution reveals independent firing patterns that emerge and evolve as the cultures mature.








ABSTRACT
Longitudinal electrophysiological recordings of neuronal networks are essential for studying network maturation, plasticity, and pharmacological responses. Yet, current microelectrode array (MEA) approaches are limited by evaporation‐induced drift in culture conditions, exacerbated by heat dissipation from active recording electronics on CMOS‐based high‐density MEAs. We present a cell culture lid featuring a water compartment at its interface that eliminates evaporation whilst maintaining gas exchange. Combined with a custom incubator that uses independent temperature control of the MEA to prevent condensation, the system enables stable, uninterrupted recordings for weeks. We show that perturbations in firing rate and functional connectivity following medium exchange are significantly reduced by suppressing evaporation. We demonstrate continuous 35‐day recordings of patterned human iPSC‐derived neuronal networks with a single half‐medium exchange, revealing multiple spatiotemporal firing patterns that are held concurrently and evolve over weeks. All design files are provided, enabling adoption across culturing platforms for longitudinal studies of development within individual cultures, and establishing the conditions required for studies of plasticity and chronic pharmacology.

title: Local chromatin, 3D genome folding and transposon cargo shape Sleeping Beauty transposition
authors: Moene, C. J. I., Eder, M., Dauban, L., Yanez-Cuna, J. O., Kocher, A. A., Eschauzier, L., Verkuilen, M., Franceschini-Santos, V. H., van Steensel, B.
abstract: The cut-and-paste DNA transposon Sleeping Beauty (SB) is widely used for genome engineering, mutagenesis and gene delivery. When mobilized from a genomic donor position ("launch site"), SB preferentially reintegrates locally (< 2 Mb), but factors governing its transposition from genomic sites remain incompletely understood. Here we analysed local transposition experiments in mouse embryonic stem cells to determine the influence of chromatin context and transposon cargo on SB transposition. Transposons in launch sites with transcriptionally active, accessible chromatin showed lower transposition efficiency. Large cargo and cargo with higher transcriptional activity also result in reduced transposition efficiency. After excision, local reintegration patterns closely resembled 3D contact frequencies of the launch site. This indicates that chromosome folding is a major determinant of the transposition pattern. Surprisingly, we did not detect any effect of the destination chromatin composition on reintegration efficiency. Cargo sequence modified the reintegration patterns: promoter-containing cargo increased both very proximal (<10kb) and interchromosomal transpositions, while CTCF binding sites in the cargo increased reintegration on the launch chromosome. Together, these results define key determinants of SB transposition in chromosomes and inform the design of SB-based genome engineering strategies.

title: Transcriptional contingency in the early hematopoiesis of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes
authors: De la Cruz, A. A., Siliceo, P., Juarez Figueroa, U., Frias, S., LealAnaya, P., Rodriguez Gomez, A. d. J.
abstract: The inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFS) are a group of heterogeneous genetic diseases caused by germline pathogenic variants in genes involved in hematopoiesis and genomic integrity. Despite sharing common phenotypical manifestations that have aided opportune diagnosis, such as bone marrow failure, congenital malformations and an increased predisposition to develop cancer, little is known about the shared and distinctive transcriptional programs in their hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells compartment that underlie the clinical manifestations of each disease. In this work we have successfully integrated and analyzed the publicly available scRNAseq datasets of HSPCs from patients with Fanconi anemia (FA) and Telomere Biology disorders (TBD), as well as healthy controls. Once integrated, we performed quality control metrics, as well as batch effect correction using different methods. Through dimensionality reduction, cell clustering and cell type annotation we found distinctive gene expression profiles per syndrome and per cell type, as well as orchestrated gene expression profiles, including upregulation of inflammatory pathways and cell proliferation pathways. This work shows the integration of datasets from FA and TBD, two major IBMFS, and provides the basis for an accumulative, comparative, and integrated atlas of scRNAseq data from patients with IBMFS.

title: Aging reshapes cardiac extravascular leukocyte transcription through bidirectional remodeling during LPS-induced endotoxemia
authors: Yu, Q., Gao, H., Fang, F., Du, J., Wang, M.
abstract: Sepsis disproportionately affects older adults and is frequently complicated by cardiac dysfunction. However, how aging alters the transcriptional responses of cardiac extravascular immune cells during systemic inflammation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated aging-dependent transcriptional remodeling of cardiac immune cells using an LPS-induced endotoxemia model in young and aged C57BL/6 mice. Mice received intraperitoneal LPS (5 mg/kg body weight) or vehicle, and cardiac extravascular leukocytes were isolated from ex vivo retrogradely perfused hearts 24 h later for single-cell RNA sequencing. Aging was associated with bidirectional transcriptional remodeling, characterized by both up- and downregulation of gene programs, particularly in cardiac macrophages, monocyte-like macrophages, T cells, and B cells following LPS challenge. A shared feature across these four cell populations was reduced representation of mitochondrial-associated transcriptional programs, indicating aging-dependent remodeling of mitochondrial biology across cardiac myeloid and lymphoid lineages during systemic inflammation. In parallel, cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling revealed distinct functional-associated responses. Macrophages and monocyte-like macrophages exhibited increased tissue-remodeling and repair-associated transcriptional programs. Both T and B cells showed reduced metabolic programs but increased actin cytoskeleton organization.
